key_insight: A spin-orbit-coupled DFTB model enables rapid screening of bismuth’s topological properties at approximately 1,000 times the computational efficiency of standard DFT.
engineering_relevance: The model makes large-scale exploration of strain and buckling practical for identifying promising bismuth-based topological structures.
method: Develop a transferable bismuth DFTB model with explicit spin-orbit coupling.
Map bismuthene band-gap closure and band inversion across strain and buckling.
Validate electronic, vibrational, energetic, and topological predictions against DFT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate rhombohedral band structures, transferability tests on phonons and additional solid phases, and DFT validation of optimized bilayer geometries, band inversion, and the Z₂ invariant.
watch_item: Validation is specific to bismuth; applying the approach to other elements or untested structural regimes requires additional parameterization and benchmarking.
paper_title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
